title: fastpath: add gating and precision-toggle with safe-mode fallback for KV scheduler
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: fastpath codepaths in the serving runtime improve latency/cost but introduce subtle correctness tradeoffs for certain kv cache and scheduler interactions when operating under mixed precision and aggressive batching. This PR implements a gating and precision-toggle system with an explicit safe-mode fallback so we can enable fastpath optimizations by default while maintaining correctness for edge cases and providing a clear rollback/fallback path.

What this changes: adds a fastpath gating layer in the runtime scheduler, a precision-toggle shim that can force FP32 fallback for specific transformer kernels at runtime, and a safe-mode fallback that triggers when deterministic checks detect kv-cache mismatches or KV scheduler starvation. The change includes instrumentation metrics and a small opt-in config surface to control gating thresholds and safe-mode sensitivity.

Notes on tradeoffs: default behavior is to attempt fastpath with mixed precision (FP16/INT8 where available) and continuous batching enabled. If the gating layer observes either 1) kernel-level verification failures, 2) unexpected kv index divergence during warmup frames, or 3) repeated scheduler preemption that would cause out-of-order KV population, the runtime will flip the precision-toggle to a conservative FP32 codepath and enable safe-mode to disable the fastpath until the condition subsides. This minimizes impact to latency-sensitive workloads while protecting correctness-critical customers.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for the gating logic, integration tests that simulate kv-cache divergence and scheduler race scenarios, and a small perf benchmark harness to validate that fastpath yields expected latency improvements when safe-mode is inactive. We ran the benchmark across T4, A100, and RTX6000 profiles and observed median token latency reductions of ~18-28% on synthetic generation workloads with steady state batching.

Deployment plan: rollout behind a feature flag. Initial rollout to internal dedicated clusters for 2 weeks with increased tracing and metric thresholds, then progressive enablement for hosted API routes that are low-risk. The PR includes a doc blurb for runtime tuning in docs/perf-tuning.md.

Related: ENG-3124 (fastpath CI perf), ENG-3180 (kv-cache correctness incidents), SUP-721 (customer report about rare hallucination/regression correlated with mixed-precision fastpath).

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Can you explain how often the verifier runs and the perf overhead? If we run verification on every warmup token this could negate fastpath gains.

Asha Patel: The verifier runs on warmup frames only (first 2-4 tokens per new KV segment) and is disabled after a short success window. We added sampling and adaptive backoff to keep overhead <2% in steady state; bench numbers are included in benchmarks/fastpath_bench.rs.
Zoe Chen: We're concerned about statefulness across multiple requests for the same session. If safe-mode flips on one request, do we pin the session?

Asha Patel: Safe-mode is session-local and timeboxed (default 30s) with an optional session pinning flag for enterprise customers. The policy is configurable via runtime config and surfaced in the console. Added tests for timebox behavior.
Priya Desai: Need a rollback plan if we see regression in the wild. Also request more telemetry around why safe-mode triggered (kernel error vs kv mismatch vs scheduler).

Asha Patel: Added detailed trigger labels to metrics (safe_mode_trigger=kernel|kv_mismatch|scheduler) and a toggle to force immediate FP32 fallback for affected hosts. Rollback plan: feature-flag off and hotfix that disables fastpath gating if needed.
ci_summary: Benchmarks: pass (internal perf job recorded improvements)
release_notes: Introduce fastpath gating and precision-toggle with safe-mode fallback for KV scheduler. Improves token latency on mixed-precision kernels while protecting correctness via verifier-based fallbacks and session-scoped safe-mode. Feature is behind a flag and configurable via runtime config.
notes: Follow-up work: add dynamic telemetry-driven thresholds for gating, expand kernel verifier coverage, and experiment with lower-cost verification sampling to further reduce warmup overhead.
